text.p: Several brokerage houses lowered their ratings and earnings forecasts for Pernod-Ricard after the drinks group reported a drop in first-half operating profit.

Portfolio managers said SGE Delahaye cut its rating to underperform from outperform on the share, Paribas Capital Markets cut its rating to hold from buy, Leven to reduce from buy and Exane to reinforce from buy.
Pernod's stock was one of the biggest losers on the Paris bourse on Friday, shedding 4.53 percent to 280.50 francs at 1440 GMT.
Leven cut its earnings forecast for the group to 22.4 francs per share for 1996 from 22.80, and to 23.50 francs from 24.50 for 1997. Portfolio managers said Paribas also cut its earnings forecasts.
Pernod-Ricard announced a 2.9 million franc rise in first-half net attributable profit to 504 million francs but a 2.4 percent drop in operating profit to 771 million.

SGE Delahaye said it may change its forecast, depending on the terms of planned alcohol tax increases. The group said it expected to pass on increases in alcohol tax announced in the French 1997 budget.
